applicant_utility.summary: 40 two-year scholarships of €20,000 gross in total (€10,000 a year) plus exemption from tuition except the first instalment each year, for international first-year students on Turin's open-access English-taught Laurea Magistrale programmes. There is no scholarship application at all: you enter the competition by applying through apply.unito.it for up to two eligible programmes, so your admission application is your scholarship application. Two awards go to each programme on a 50-point scale with a 36-point eligibility threshold, and each of the four instalments is gated on specific credit and weighted-average milestones, so the money arrives in tranches rather than as a lump sum.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants under 30 with a non-Italian master's-qualifying degree, B2 English, who are not resident in Italy and are applying to an open-access English-taught Turin master's programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme appears in article 2 of the call and is open access and English-taught; application or numerical-admission programmes are out of scope
Prepare the admission application for the first programme as if it were the scholarship application itself, including any test or interview
Check your B2 English position in advance, since English knowledge is one of the four scored criteria even though no certificate is demanded
Keep your age in view: the tie-break is the younger candidate, and age also feeds residency and planning calculations
Prepare the Italian visa and Universitaly pre-enrolment timeline early, since the award is only disbursed once matriculation is complete and the permit request is submitted
common_rejection_risks: Being resident in Italy at application, which includes non-EU citizens holding a valid enrolment permit
Holding Italian citizenship, including dual citizenship, since Italian citizenship prevails
Already being enrolled, or having been enrolled, in a degree programme at UniTo or another university, including a simultaneous enrolment
Applying after the first year, for a course transfer or as a transfer student from another university
Falling below the 36-point eligibility threshold, or being the third-best candidate in a programme where only two awards exist
Applying only to numerical-admission (restricted-access) programmes, which are not covered by this call
Missing the 10-day acceptance window, which forfeits the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The first instalment of tuition fees for each academic year, the Italian visa and permit costs, and flights to Italy.
document_audit: No additional documents beyond the admission application are required, so the admission file carries the scholarship evaluation
Candidatures sent by email, and multiple applications using different apply@unito profiles, are disregarded
Payment is made to an Italian current account or prepaid card with an Italian IBAN held or co-held by the student, so a bank account must be opened in Italy
Fraudulent declarations are a criminal offence and every document is verified by expert staff
alerts: Unassigned scholarships cannot be redistributed to other programmes, so programme choice genuinely changes your odds rather than just your field
Rankings run per degree programme, not centrally, and no personal communications are sent - check the University website from 14 May 2026
The June 2026 ranking is published in English, which is worth checking as evidence of how the notice reaches applicants
Ranking scroll stops on 30 November 2026, after which vacant awards are not reallocated
Credits earned through career abbreviation are not counted towards the instalment thresholds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one or two applications through apply.unito.it between 25 November and 29 January, complete any admission test or interview, watch for the per-programme ranking from 14 May 2026, then return the signed acceptance letter within 10 days and complete matriculation, visa and Italian bank account set-up.

applicant_utility.summary: Three two-year UNHCR-supported scholarships for refugee students resident in 13 listed African and Asian countries, worth €7,000 a year plus exemption from essentially all enrolment charges, university accommodation and a broad package of health, permit and settlement support. Applications go through the single UNICORE portal at universitycorridors.unhcr.it by 17 April 2026 at noon Italian time, and selection has two distinct gates: a documentation and CV score that must reach 25 out of 40 just to reach the interview, and then an interview that must push you to 40 out of 80 overall. Note the trap that you must not be pre-enrolled on Universitaly at any other Italian university, which rules out hedging across corridors.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Refugee students resident in one of the 13 corridor countries who hold a bachelor's degree awarded between January 2021 and April 2026 with a GPA of 3.0 or an average of at least 24/30, and have never studied at UniTo or a UNICORE partner.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your refugee status was obtained in your country of residence in collaboration with UNHCR, since UNHCR verifies it on site before the interview
Convert your average into the Italian system using the official Ministry of Education formula on universitycorridors.unhcr.it/admission-criteria and check you clear 3.0 or 24/30
Check your degree date falls between 01 January 2021 and 17 April 2026
Write the motivational letter in English and prepare a CV that shows professional experience and skills, which are separately scored
Verify you are not pre-enrolled on Universitaly at another Italian university, which disqualifies you
Collect the Refugee Identity card or Proof of Registration and the stamped, signed transcript with an official translation into English or Italian
common_rejection_risks: Residing in a country not on the 13-country list, which is a hard eligibility bar
A qualification awarded outside the 01/01/2021 to 17/04/2026 window
A GPA below 3.0 or an average below 24/30 after conversion
Never having been enrolled at UNITO or another UNICORE partner university - a second corridor entry is barred
Being pre-enrolled on Universitaly at another Italian university
Documents submitted in a format other than PDF or not legible, which is an explicit exclusion ground
Submitting an incomplete application, sending it by email, using multiple email addresses, or trying to modify it after submission
Missing the 10 July 2026 acceptance deadline, or failing to complete matriculation, visa and permit steps in time
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to Italy and any costs before arrival other than the €100 first-necessity payment; the scholarship is not compatible with any other scholarship from public or private institutions.
document_audit: Everything must be PDF and legible; the transcript needs the stamp and signature of the issuing institution
Once submitted, the application cannot be modified, so assemble the file completely before you press send
Bring the Ration Card Number or Refugee Identity Card to the online interview, since it is checked
You will need an Italian bank account with an IBAN held or co-held by you, plus a signed financial contract, before the first €3,000 instalment is released
alerts: Only eligible applications proceed to the selection stages, and failing the degree-programme admission step automatically excludes you from the scholarship selection
The tie-break favours female candidates and younger candidates, so a marginally tied position can still resolve favourably
Results appear on the University portal from 22 June 2026 with no personal notification

The corridor is jointly run by UniTo, UNHCR, MAECI, Unione Pastorale Migranti, Camminare Insieme and the Commissione Sinodale per la Diaconia, so services come from several organisations rather than the university alone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply at universitycorridors.unhcr.it by 17 April 2026 at noon Italian time with all documents in legible PDF, complete the qualification evaluation and UNHCR status check, attend the online interview with your ration card or refugee ID, then check the University portal from 22 June 2026 and accept by 10 July 2026 before matriculating, obtaining the visa and arriving in Italy.
